claim: Pediatric diffuse midline gliomas (pDMG) are an aggressive type of childhood cancer with a fatal outcome.
source: Pediatric diffuse midline gliomas (pDMG) are an aggressive type of childhood cancer with a fatal outcome.
evidence: This is a general characterization statement supported by established scientific knowledge about pDMG.

claim: K27M mutations in histone H3 are a major epigenetic determinant of pDMG.
source: Their major epigenetic determinism has become clear, notably with the identification of K27M mutations in histone H3.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about the role of K27M mutations in pDMG.

claim: 20 to 30% of pDMG cases have an altered BMP signaling pathway with an oncogenic mutation on the BMP type I receptor ALK2, encoded by ACVR1.
source: In 20 to 30% of cases, these tumors have an altered BMP signaling pathway with an oncogenic mutation on the BMP type I receptor ALK2, encoded by ACVR1.
evidence: This is a statistical claim about the frequency of ACVR1 mutations in pDMG, supported by established knowledge.

claim: The BMP signaling pathway is activated at similar levels between ACVR1 wild-type and mutant tumors.
source: By integrating bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data, we show here that the BMP signaling pathway is activated at similar levels between ACVR1 wild-type and mutant tumors
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data from patient samples.

claim: BMP2 and BMP7 are putative activators of the BMP pathway in a specific subpopulation of pDMG cells.
source: By integrating bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data, we show here that the BMP signaling pathway is activated at similar levels between ACVR1 wild-type and mutant tumors and identify BMP2 and BMP7 as putative activators of the pathway in a specific subpopulation of cells.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data.

claim: BMP2/7 synergizes with H3.3K27M to induce a transcriptomic rewiring associated with a quiescent but invasive cell state.
source: By using both pediatric isogenic glioma lines genetically modified to overexpress H3.3K27M and patients-derived DIPG cell lines, we demonstrate that BMP2/7 synergizes with H3.3K27M to induce a transcriptomic rewiring associated with a quiescent but invasive cell state.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell line models.

claim: pDMG are almost uniformly fatal, with a median overall survival of 9–11 months.
source: pDMG are almost uniformly fatal, with a median overall survival of 9–11 months (Khuong-Quang et al., 2012; Hoffman et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: pDMG represent the leading cause of mortality in pediatric neuro-oncology.
source: thereby representing the leading cause of mortality in pediatric neuro-oncology (Mackay et al., 2017; Sulman and Eisenstat, 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Radiotherapy is the current standard of care for pDMG and is at best only transiently effective.
source: Radiotherapy, the current standard of care, is at best only transiently effective (Sulman and Eisenstat, 2021; Vitanza and Monje, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: pDMG are highly resistant to currently available chemotherapies.
source: Moreover, pDMG are highly resistant to currently available chemotherapies although promising combinations of molecules, including ONC201, are currently in clinical trials (Jackson et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: 80% of pDMG cases result from a lysine-to-methionine substitution at position 27 (K27M) in genes encoding histone variants H3.3 or H3.1.
source: High-throughput sequencing demonstrated that pDMG is associated with a major disruption of the epigenetic landscape, resulting in 80% of cases from a lysine-to-methionine substitution at position 27 (K27M) in genes encoding histone variants H3.3 (H3F3A/H3-3A) or H3.1 (HIST1H3B/H3C2 or HIST1H3C/H3C3) (Khuong-Quang et al., 2012; Schwartzentruber et al., 2012; Sturm et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: H3K27M variants are affine for EZH2, the methyltransferase subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and inhibit its activity.
source: H3K27M variants, also known as oncohistones, are affine for EZH2, the methyltransferase subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) and inhibit its activity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic statement supported by established knowledge about H3K27M function.

claim: pDMG show abnormal methyl group deposition on H3K27 and a global loss of trimethylated H3K27 (H3K27me3).
source: As a result, pDMG show abnormal methyl group deposition on H3K27 and a global loss of trimethylated H3K27 (H3K27me3) (Bender et al., 2013; Chan et al., 2013; Lewis et al., 2013; Piunti et al., 2017; Stafford et al., 2018; Harutyunyan et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: H3K27me3 is a histone mark associated with transcriptional repression.
source: a global loss of trimethylated H3K27 (H3K27me3) (Bender et al., 2013; Chan et al., 2013; Lewis et al., 2013; Piunti et al., 2017; Stafford et al., 2018; Harutyunyan et al., 2019), a histone mark associated with transcriptional repression.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the function of H3K27me3.

claim: 20 to 30% of pDMG cases are associated with mutations in the ACVR1 gene.
source: Accordingly, 20 to 30% of pDMG cases are associated with mutations in the ACVR1 gene, encoding for the bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) type I receptor ALK2 (Buczkowicz et al., 2014; Fontebasso et al., 2014; Taylor et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: ACVR1 mutations lead to the overactivation of intracellular BMP signaling pathway.
source: which leads to the overactivation of intracellular BMP signaling pathway (Carvalho et al., 2019; Fortin et al., 2020; Haupt et al., 2018; Hoeman et al., 2019; Ramachandran et al., 2021; Jessa et al., 2022; Mucha et al., 2018; Hatsell et al., 2015; Hino et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies.

claim: Increased BMP signaling in the pDMG epigenetic context promotes tumorigenesis by maintaining cells in a proliferative, mesenchymal-like, and undifferentiated state in vitro and in vivo.
source: Such increase in BMP signaling in the pDMG epigenetic context has been suggested to promote tumorigenesis by maintaining cells in a proliferative, mesenchymal-like, and undifferentiated state in vitro and in vivo (Carvalho et al., 2019; Fortin et al., 2020; Hoeman et al., 2019; Jessa et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: In 69% of cases, ACVR1 mutations are associated with the H3.1K27M mutation.
source: In 69% of cases, these ACVR1 mutations are associated with the H3.1K27M mutation, whereas less than 20% are observed in H3.3K27M tumors (Mackay et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Less than 20% of ACVR1 mutations are observed in H3.3K27M tumors.
source: In 69% of cases, these ACVR1 mutations are associated with the H3.1K27M mutation, whereas less than 20% are observed in H3.3K27M tumors (Mackay et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: H3.1K27M tumors mutated for ACVR1 emerge from a ventral pool of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPC) characterized by the expression of the transcription factor NKX6-1 and dependent on the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling.
source: Recent data support the idea that H3.1K27M tumors mutated for ACVR1 would emerge from a ventral pool of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPC) characterized by the expression of the transcription factor NKX6-1 and dependent on the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) signaling (Jessa et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: H3.3K27M tumors preferentially derive from dorsal progenitors expressing the dorsal PAX3- and BMP-dependent transcription factor.
source: In contrast, H3.3K27M is thought to preferentially derive from dorsal progenitors expressing the dorsal PAX3- and BMP-dependent transcription factor (Jessa et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: BMP ligands may exert a tumor-suppressive activity in H3.3K27M-ACVR1 wild-type (WT) pDMG cellular models.
source: However, while the pro-tumorigenic activity of BMP signaling is clear in ACVR1 mutant pDMG, recent data have unexpectedly reported that BMP ligands may exert a tumor-suppressive activity in H3.3K27M-ACVR1 wild-type (WT) pDMG cellular models (Sun et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Principal component analysis (PCA) performed on BMP target genes demonstrates no segregation of ACVR1 mutant from ACVR1 WT samples in two independent publicly available transcriptomic cohorts.
source: Principal component analysis (PCA) performed on this BMP target genes subset demonstrates no segregation of ACVR1 mutant (in blue) from ACVR1 WT samples (in red) in two independent publicly available transcriptomic cohorts of 31 (McLeod et al., 2021) and 40 (Mackay et al., 2017) patients (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The expression pattern of BMP target genes does not segregate pDMG according to their ACVR1 status in an unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis in both cohorts.
source: Consistently, the expression pattern of these genes does not segregate pDMG according to their ACVR1 status in an unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis in both cohorts (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There is no significant difference in the TGF-β/BMP activation PROGENy score between ACVR1 mutant and WT tumors.
source: Interestingly, we observed no significant difference in the TGF-β/BMP activation PROGENy score between ACVR1 mutant and WT tumors (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data using the PROGENy method and is shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The TGF-β/BMP PROGENy score was higher than the maximum observed in ACVR1 mutant tumors in 12.5 (cohort 2)–18.5% (cohort 1) of ACVR1 WT pDMG.
source: Of note, although variable, this score was even higher than the maximum observed in ACVR1 mutant tumors in 12.5 (cohort 2)–18.5% (cohort 1) of ACVR1 WT pDMG.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data.

claim: Several BMP ligands, receptors, antagonists and intracellular transducers are expressed in ACVR1 WT pDMG at expression levels very similar to those observed in ACVR1 mutant tumors.
source: Compatible with BMP signaling being active, several ligands, receptors, antagonists and intracellular transducers are expressed in ACVR1 WT pDMG, albeit at expression levels very similar to those observed in ACVR1 mutant tumors (Figure 1B and D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1B, 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: CHRDL1 is significantly overexpressed in ACVR1 WT tumors compared to mutant ones in two independent transcriptomic cohorts.
source: By differential analysis, we found that only CHRDL1 is significantly overexpressed in ACVR1 WT tumors compared to mutant ones in two independent transcriptomic cohorts, as previously reported in pDMG cell lines (Sun et al., 2022; Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' differential analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D. It is also supported by a citation.

claim: BMP2 and BMP7 are the two most highly expressed ligands in H3.3K27M pDMG in both cohorts with no significant difference according to H3 and ACVR1 mutational status.
source: Out of all BMP ligands present in pDMG tumors, BMP2 and BMP7 are the two most highly expressed ligands in H3.3K27M pDMG in both cohorts with no significant difference according to H3 and ACVR1 mutational status (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: BMP7 is only expressed at E13.5 during embryogenesis and is then progressively re-expressed post-natally from P14 notably in the pontine hindbrain, to reach a maximum in most territories including prosomere 2 at P28.
source: By analyzing data from the ALLEN Developing Mouse Brain Atlas (Lein et al., 2007), we observed that BMP7 is only expressed at E13.5 during embryogenesis. It is then progressively re-expressed post-natally from P14 notably in the pontine hindbrain, to reach a maximum in most territories including prosomere 2 at P28, which is compatible with the spatio-temporal window of occurrence of H3.3K27M pDMG tumors (Jessa et al., 2022; Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of data from the ALLEN Developing Mouse Brain Atlas and is shown in Figure 1G.

claim: BMP2 is only expressed at the E18.5 embryonic stage.
source: BMP2 is only expressed at the E18.5 embryonic stage and BMP4 expression peaks at P14 corresponding to infancy (Burford, 2021), before decreasing during the post-natal period in these territories (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of developmental brain data and is shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: BMP4 expression peaks at P14 corresponding to infancy, before decreasing during the post-natal period.
source: BMP2 is only expressed at the E18.5 embryonic stage and BMP4 expression peaks at P14 corresponding to infancy (Burford, 2021), before decreasing during the post-natal period in these territories (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of developmental brain data and is shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: BMP7 expression gradually increases to reach its maximum in the midline structure in the mid-childhood period.
source: Similarly, by integrating transcriptomic data from the HBT program (Kang et al., 2011), we observed that BMP7 expression but not BMP2 and BMP4 gradually increases to reach its maximum in the midline structure in the mid-childhood period (green curve, Figure 1F, G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G), then coinciding with the peak incidence of pDMG tumors (Mackay et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of data from the HBT program and is shown in Figure 1F, G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: BMP7 expression significantly decreases after H3.3K27M induction in both SF188 and Res259 cells.
source: Interestingly, BMP7 expression significantly decreases after H3.3K27M induction in both SF188 and Res259 cells (Figure 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell line models and is shown in Figure 2A.

claim: BMP2 expression is increased after H3.3K27M induction in both SF188 and Res259 cells.
source: whereas BMP2 and BMP4 expressions are respectively increased or unmodified (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell line models and is shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: BMP4 expression is unmodified after H3.3K27M induction in both SF188 and Res259 cells.
source: whereas BMP2 and BMP4 expressions are respectively increased or unmodified (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell line models and is shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: BMP7 treatment leads to a significant increase in BMP targets expression in both H3.3K27M-Res259 and -SF188 cells compared to H3.3 WT cell lines, with at least a twofold increase at 3 and 24 hr for both ID1 and ID2.
source: Using qRT-PCR as a first hint, we observed a significant increase in BMP targets expression following BMP7 treatment in both H3.3K27M-Res259 and -SF188 cells compared to H3.3 WT cell lines, with at least a twofold increase at 3 and 24 hr for both ID1 and ID2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from cell line models and is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Both levels and kinetics of SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation in H3.3K27M versus WT overexpressing cells remain unchanged, indicating that BMP canonical pathway activation is not modified by histone mutational status.
source: Interestingly, both levels and kinetics of SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation in H3.3K27M versus WT overexpressing cells remain unchanged, indicating that BMP canonical pathway activation is not modified by histone mutational status (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from cell line models and is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The increase in TGF-β/BMP activation score induced by BMP7 is potentiated and remains significantly higher at 24 hr in H3.3K27M-Res259 compared to their wild-type counterparts.
source: Using PROGENy analysis, we observed that the increase in TGF-β/BMP activation score induced by BMP7 is potentiated and remains significantly higher at 24 hr in H3.3K27M-Res259 compared to their wild-type counterparts (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analyzed with PROGENy and is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A subset of 900 genes appears differentially expressed specifically between treated and untreated H3.3K27M-Res259 cells, but not in H3.3 WT ones.
source: While differentially expressed genes at 3 hr mostly correspond to the expression of the K27M mutation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, F), a subset of 900 genes appears differentially expressed (DE) specifically between treated and untreated H3.3K27M-Res259 cells, but not in H3.3 WT ones (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, F.

claim: Differentially expressed genes between treated and untreated H3.3K27M-Res259 cells are notably associated with alteration in cell cycle regulation.
source: Enrichment analyses revealed that DE genes are notably associated with alteration in cell cycle regulation (Figure 2D–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: The downregulated genes in H3.3K27M BMP7-treated cells correspond to E2F targets.
source: and that the downregulated ones in H3.3K27M BMP7-treated cells correspond to E2F targets (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: BMP7 treatment leads to a significant 12.2% and 16.7% increase of cells in the G0/G1 phase, respectively in H3.3K27M-SF188 and -Res259 cells, while its effect is limited to a 3% and 10.3% increase in their WT counterparts.
source: Consistently, BMP7 treatment leads to a significant 12.2% and 16.7% increase of cells in the G0/G1 phase, respectively in H3.3K27M-SF188 and -Res259 cells, while its effect is limited to a 3% and 10.3% increase in their WT counterparts (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data and is shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The number of H3.3K27M-Res259 cells is significantly reduced by 1.7-fold compared to non-treated cells upon BMP7 treatment, while the decrease is limited to 1.2-fold in WT ones.
source: Similarly, the number of H3.3K27M-Res259 cells is significantly reduced by 1.7-fold compared to non-treated cells upon BMP7 treatment, while the decrease is limited to 1.2-fold in WT ones (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting data and is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The K27M-dependent BMP7 effect is associated with a significant 1.8-fold increase in cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 1 A (CDKN1A, encoding P21) expression.
source: Of note, this K27M-dependent BMP7 effect is associated with a significant 1.8-fold increase in cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 1 A (CDKN1A, encoding P21; Figure 2G) expression
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The K27M-dependent BMP7 effect is associated with a reciprocal decrease in RB1 phosphorylation.
source: and a reciprocal decrease in RB1 phosphorylation (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data and is shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The cell cycle blockade induced by BMP7 in H3.3K27M cells is unlikely to result from the entry of cells in senescence since there is no difference in beta-galactosidase activity (SA-β-gal) between wild-type and mutant cells upon BMP7 treatment.
source: This cell cycle blockade is unlikely to result from the entry of cells in senescence since there is no difference in beta-galactosidase activity (SA-β-gal) between wild-type and mutant cells upon BMP7 treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by SA-β-gal activity assay data and is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Genes that correspond to cooperative effects of K27M epigenetic alterations and BMP7-mediated transcriptional regulation are involved in processes related to invasion/migration, including extracellular matrix organization, regulation of cell/neuron projection, and adhesion.
source: Interestingly, enrichment analyses revealed that these genes are involved in processes related to invasion/migration, including extracellular matrix organization, regulation of cell/neuron projection, and adhesion (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Some genes such as ITGA2, ROBO2, and MMP28 are already induced following H3.3K27M expression, and their expression is further amplified by the BMP7 treatment.
source: Some of these genes such as ITGA2, ROBO2, and MMP28 are already induced following H3.3K27M expression, and their expression is further amplified by the BMP7 treatment (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2J.

claim: COL28A1 is specifically induced or repressed by the K27M+BMP7 context.
source: Conversely, others, such as COL28A1, are specifically induced or repressed by the K27M+BMP7 context (Figure 2J), consistently with our decision tree algorithm.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 2J.

claim: Expression of the H3.3K27M mutation is sufficient to drive a moderate increase in invasion compared to the WT context.
source: Expression of the H3.3K27M mutation is sufficient to drive a moderate increase in invasion compared to the WT context.
evidence: This claim is supported by invasion assay data.

claim: The invasive effect of H3.3K27M is largely amplified by BMP7, with a global 5.6-fold in the H3.3 mutant context, compared to twofold in the H3.3 WT one.
source: However, this phenomenon is largely amplified by BMP7, with a global 5.6-fold in the H3.3 mutant context, compared to twofold in the H3.3 WT one.
evidence: This claim is supported by invasion assay data.

claim: BMP7 is the most expressed ligand in two ACVR1 WT/H3.3K27M DIPG cell lines.
source: First, we observed that BMP7 is the most expressed ligand in two ACVR1 WT/H3.3K27M DIPG cell lines, but that few if any other BMP ligands, including BMP4, are (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from DIPG cell lines and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BMP2 expression is notably low in ACVR1 WT/H3.3K27M DIPG cell lines.
source: Unlike in tumors, BMP2 expression is notably low in these cell lines (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from DIPG cell lines and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Exposure of ACVR1 WT H3.3K27M DIPG cells to hypoxia or ONC201 are both sufficient to induce a significant increase in BMP2 expression.
source: Accordingly, exposure of ACVR1 WT H3.3K27M DIPG cells to hypoxia or ONC201, which is known to significantly increase ROS production (Przystal et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2023), are both sufficient to induce a significant increase in BMP2 expression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from DIPG cell lines and is shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Treatment of DIPG spheroids with increasing doses of recombinant human BMP2 triggers SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation.
source: As shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C, treatment of DIPG spheroids with increasing doses of recombinant human BMP2 triggers SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from DIPG spheroids and is shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Treatment of DIPG spheroids with increasing doses of recombinant human BMP2 leads to a strong dose-dependent decrease in growth rate.
source: and leads to a strong dose-dependent decrease in growth rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by growth monitoring data from DIPG spheroids.

claim: Ki67 staining is significantly decreased upon BMP2 treatment in DIPG spheroids.
source: Consistently, Ki67 staining, a marker of proliferation, is significantly decreased upon BMP2 treatment (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from DIPG spheroids and is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment of DIPG-spheroids with the BMP inhibitor LDN-193189 (LDN) leads to a slight increase in KI67-positive cells.
source: Reciprocally, treatment of DIPG-spheroids with the BMP inhibitor LDN-193189 (LDN) leads to a slight increase in KI67-positive cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from DIPG spheroids and is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The effect of BMP2 on Ki67 staining was largely mitigated in BT245 and DIPGXIII cell lines in which the K27M mutant allele was removed, indicating that it may depend on the K27M-specific epigenetic context.
source: This effect was largely mitigated in BT245 and DIPGXIII cell lines in which the K27M mutant allele was removed (Harutyunyan et al., 2019), indicating that it may depend on the K27M-specific epigenetic context (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth monitoring data from DIPG cell lines and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The combined knock-out of K27M and BMP inhibition with LDN treatment resulted in the failure of pDMG cells to proliferate and form gliospheres.
source: Of particular interest, the combined knock-out of K27M and BMP inhibition with LDN treatment resulted in the failure of pDMG cells to proliferate and form gliospheres (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth monitoring data from DIPG cell lines and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: BMP2 significantly increases the migration of tumor cells from Matrigel-embedded 3D-DIPG spheroids.
source: BMP2 significantly increases the migration of tumor cells from Matrigel-embedded 3D-DIPG spheroids, while an antagonistic effect was observed upon LDN treatment (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by invasion assay data from DIPG spheroids and is shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: LDN treatment has an antagonistic effect on the migration of tumor cells from Matrigel-embedded 3D-DIPG spheroids.
source: BMP2 significantly increases the migration of tumor cells from Matrigel-embedded 3D-DIPG spheroids, while an antagonistic effect was observed upon LDN treatment (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by invasion assay data from DIPG spheroids and is shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The BMP-responsive pool of tumor cells correlates significantly with BMP receptors expression, in particular to BMPR2, BMPR1B, BMPR1A, and ACVR1 levels, respectively in 8, 5, 5, and 4 out of 10 samples.
source: Integration of all these data unveiled that the BMP-responsive (i.e. High PROGENy TGF-β/BMP score) pool of tumor cells correlates significantly with BMP receptors expression, in particular to BMPR2, BMPR1B, BMPR1A, and ACVR1 levels, respectively in 8, 5, 5, and 4 out of 10 samples (Figure 3E–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data analysis and is shown in Figure 3E-F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The BMP-responsive pool of cells is significantly enriched in genes involved in positive regulation of cell migration and in cell-matrix adhesion.
source: Interestingly, this BMP-responsive pool of cells is significantly enriched in genes involved in positive regulation of cell migration and in cell-matrix adhesion (Figure 3G)
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of scRNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The BMP-responsive pool of cells shows a specific quiescent-compatible decrease in genes involved in transcription/translation processes.
source: while showing a specific quiescent-compatible decrease in genes involved in transcription/translation processes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by enrichment analysis of scRNA-seq data and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The most highly expressed BMP ligands in pDMG tumors are BMP2 and BMP7 along with BMP8B.
source: Consistently with observations in bulk and single-cell analyses of patients' tumors/models, the most highly expressed BMP ligands are BMP2 and BMP7 along with BMP8B (Supplementary file 1b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data and is shown in Supplementary file 1b and Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: BMP receptors expression correlate significantly with the invasive niche score.
source: In line with single-cell analyses, we observed on the contrary that BMP receptors expression correlate significantly with the invasive niche score defined by Ren et al., 2023 (Figure 3I)
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data analysis and is shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The invasive niche score strongly correlates to the PROGENy TGF-β/BMP score.
source: Moreover, the invasive niche score strongly correlates to the PROGENy TGF-β/BMP score (Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data analysis and is shown in Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The BMP-responsive invasive niche is characterized by a high expression of key markers of BMP activity (ID1), as well as markers of stemness (CD44, HEY1) and migration/invasion (TNC, IGFBP7, ITGAV).
source: Coherently, this BMP-responsive invasive niche is characterized by a high expression of key markers of BMP activity (ID1), as well as markers of stemness (CD44, HEY1) and migration/invasion (TNC, IGFBP7, ITGAV) (Figure 3K).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data analysis and is shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Tumor-autonomous production of BMP2 and BMP7 synergize to maintain a quiescent-invasive niche in H3.3K27M DIPG.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that tumor-autonomous production of BMP2 and BMP7 synergize to maintain a quiescent-invasive niche in H3.3K27M DIPG.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: BMP7 is sufficient to induce a transcriptomic reprogramming specific to the H3.3K27M epigenetic context, which leads to the emergence of a quiescent but invasive cell state.
source: Altogether, these data support the fact that BMP7 is sufficient to induce a transcriptomic reprogramming specific to the H3.3K27M epigenetic context, which leads to the emergence of a quiescent but invasive cell state.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The BMP pathway has a generic oncogenic role in gliomagenesis of pDMG.
source: These data suggest a generic oncogenic role for the BMP pathway in gliomagenesis of pDMG and pave the way for specific targeting of downstream effectors mediating the K27M/BMP crosstalk.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The activation of the BMP pathway in ACVR1 WT H3.3K27M tumors could be at least partially mediated by two complementary tumor-autonomous and microenvironment-dependent mechanisms.
source: By analyzing the expression of BMP effectors in pDMG tumors and patient-derived DIPG models, we propose that the activation of this pathway in ACVR1 WT H3.3K27M tumors could be at least partially mediated by two complementary tumor-autonomous and microenvironment-dependent mechanisms.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The expression of BMP, and notably BMP7, could synergize with or even trigger the autocrine production of BMP ligands by the tumors, among which BMP2 and 7.
source: Upon initiation, the expression of BMP, and notably BMP7, could synergize with or even trigger the autocrine production of BMP ligands by the tumors, among which BMP2 and 7.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the authors' data and inference.

claim: Positive feedback loops maintaining the expression of BMP ligands have been described notably during development.
source: Indeed, such positive feedback loops maintaining the expression of BMP ligands have already been described notably during development (Kozmikova et al., 2013; Christiaen et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The expression of BMP ligands is similar in ACVR1 mutant and WT tumors and independent of H3 status.
source: The fact that the expression of BMP ligands is similar in ACVR1 mutant and WT tumors and independent of H3 status (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F) suggests that this regulatory loop is involved in most tumors, but probably by different mechanisms depending on the mutational context.
evidence: This claim is supported by the authors' analysis of transcriptomic data and is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: BMP secretion by the microenvironment may prime the BMP activation in tumor cells and be required for oncogenic transformation.
source: Thus, BMP secretion by the microenvironment may prime the BMP activation in tumor cells and be required for oncogenic transformation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the authors' data and inference.

claim: The dynamic modulation of BMP2 expression in response to stresses, such as hypoxia or treatments, could synergize with constitutive production of BMP7 to drive the emergence of an aggressive cell state.
source: Once established, the dynamic modulation of BMP2 expression in response to stresses, such as hypoxia or treatments, could synergize with constitutive production of BMP7 to drive the emergence of an aggressive cell state.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on the authors' data and inference.

claim: The expression of BMP-target genes ID1 to 4 was previously reported to be strongly decreased in pDMG cell lines in which the K27M mutation was removed by CRISPR-Cas9.
source: Of note, the expression of BMP-target genes ID1 to 4 was previously reported to be strongly decreased in pDMG cell lines in which the K27M mutation was removed by CRISPR-Cas9 (Harutyunyan et al., 2019)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The maintenance of BMP activation in a pool of tumor cells relies on the specific K27M-mediated epigenetic context.
source: suggesting that even the maintenance of BMP activation in a pool of tumor cells relies on the specific K27M-mediated epigenetic context.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited study.

claim: Blocking the BMP pathway with LDN in K27M-KO cells induces tumor cell death.
source: In addition, blocking the BMP pathway with LDN in these K27M-KO cells induces tumor cell death, supporting the view that the K27M/BMP oncogenic synergy plays a major role in maintaining oncogenic potential (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and is shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The K27M/BMP oncogenic synergy plays a major role in maintaining oncogenic potential.
source: In addition, blocking the BMP pathway with LDN in these K27M-KO cells induces tumor cell death, supporting the view that the K27M/BMP oncogenic synergy plays a major role in maintaining oncogenic potential (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: BMP7 is sufficient to potentiate the entry of cells in a quiescent state in a H3.3K27M-dependent manner, via a transcriptomic switch largely relying on the downregulation of E2F-targets cell-cycle regulating genes.
source: Indeed, using a genetically engineered glioma model, we confirmed that BMP7 is sufficient to potentiate the entry of cells in a quiescent state in a H3.3K27M-dependent manner, via a transcriptomic switch largely relying on the downregulation of E2F-targets cell-cycle regulating genes.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The quiescent cellular phenotype induced by BMP7 could paradoxically constitute an aggressive treatment-resistant state.
source: Nevertheless, this quiescent cellular phenotype could paradoxically constitute an aggressive treatment-resistant state, as previously observed in adult glioblastoma (Atkins et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2012; Xie et al., 2022) and thus explaining its increase in response to treatment (Sun et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the authors' data and citations to published studies.

claim: CHRDL1 has been shown to exert BMP-independent functions in synapse plasticity and maturation.
source: Indeed, if CHRDL1 was first classified as a member of the chordin family of secreted BMP antagonists due to sequence homology, it has been shown that it exerts BMP-independent functions in synapse plasticity and maturation (Blanco-Suarez et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: CHRDL1 has been described as an activator of the BMP pathway.
source: Moreover, this protein has also been described as an activator of the BMP pathway (Lin et al., 2005)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: Different ligands of the BMP pathway may have different impacts on the cellular phenotype induced by the H3.3K27M mutation.
source: However, it cannot be ruled out also that different ligands of the BMP pathway may have different impacts on the cellular phenotype induced by the H3.3K27M mutation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging alternative possibilities.

claim: BMP4 treatment promotes the differentiation of DIPG tumor cells.
source: Accordingly, it was shown that BMP4 treatment promotes the differentiation of DIPG tumor cells, in line with its putative tumor suppressor activity (Sun et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: BMP activation by BMP2/7 in a H3.3K27M epigenetic context induces a transcriptomic switch conferring enhanced invasion potential to pDMG tumor cells.
source: However, beyond quiescence, we observed that BMP activation by BMP2/7 in a H3.3K27M epigenetic context induces a transcriptomic switch rather than conferring enhanced invasion potential to pDMG tumor cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The BMP2/7 pair has been shown to trigger BMP signaling as a heterodimer notably during embryogenesis, with a higher efficiency than homodimers.
source: Interestingly, this pair has already been shown to trigger BMP signaling as a heterodimer notably during embryogenesis, with a higher efficiency than homodimers (Kim et al., 2019; Schmid, 2000; Tajer et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Activation of the BMP pathway may be finely regulated in pDMG to be maintained at optimal pro-oncogenic levels, without triggering the tumor-suppressive effects or negative regulatory loops associated with its over-activation.
source: Keeping in mind that BMP2 appears to be dynamically regulated by tumor cells upon stress, these data suggest that activation of the BMP pathway may be finely regulated in pDMG to be maintained at optimal pro-oncogenic levels, without triggering the tumor-suppressive effects (Sun et al., 2022) or negative regulatory loops associated with its over-activation (Christiaen et al., 2010; Afrakhte et al., 1998; Akizu et al., 2010; Bénazet et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the authors' data and citations to published studies.

claim: The BMP2/7-driven cell state fits with previous results obtained in other glioma models, in which a subpopulation of quiescent cells was identified as partially responsible for tumor invasiveness.
source: The BMP2/7-driven cell state that we described here fits with previous results obtained in other glioma models, in which a subpopulation of quiescent cells was identified as partially responsible for tumor invasiveness (Atkins et al., 2019; Antonica et al., 2022; Furst et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Invasiveness is a hallmark of pDMG aggressiveness.
source: a hallmark of pDMG aggressiveness (Kluiver et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a published study.

claim: The therapeutic strategy to target the H3.3K27M/BMP crosstalk should be based on the targeting of the downstream effectors, such as ID1 or TNC.
source: Given the complexity of the phenotype induced by H3.3K27M/BMP crosstalk and the pleiotropic role of BMP proteins in the central nervous system, the therapeutic strategy to be developed should be based on the targeting of the downstream effectors, such as ID1 as recently described (Messinger et al., 2023), or TNC, which may be responsible for the invasive phenotype.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the authors' findings and a citation to a published study.
